title: Saved searches that answer real questions
goal: You will create and test a transaction saved search with filters, result columns, highlighting, recipients, and a recurring email schedule.
prerequisites: Permission to create Transaction saved searches
A defined transaction type, date range, and status to filter
Approved email recipients and delivery cadence

steps.action: Create a new Transaction saved search.
steps.where: Reports > Saved Searches > All Saved Searches, then the New Saved Search page.
steps.why: The record type determines which criteria and result fields are available.
steps.checkpoint: A Transaction Saved Search form appears with Criteria, Results, Highlighting, and Email tabs.
hint_levels: Start from the list of saved searches.
Use the New Saved Search button and choose the transaction record type.
Go to Reports > Saved Searches > All Saved Searches > New Saved Search, then click Transaction.

steps.action: Enter a unique search title and select Public only if other roles should find it.
steps.where: Search Title and Public fields in the header of the Transaction Saved Search form.
steps.why: A descriptive name makes the search identifiable without exposing it unnecessarily.
steps.checkpoint: The Search Title field contains your chosen name and the Public checkbox reflects the intended access.
hint_levels: Name the search before configuring its logic.
Use a name describing the records and purpose; leave Public cleared unless sharing is intended.
In the form header, complete Search Title, then set the Public checkbox as required.

steps.action: Add the main filters for transaction type, date, and status.
steps.where: Criteria tab > Standard subtab > Filter rows.
steps.why: These filters restrict the search to the transactions the task actually needs.
steps.checkpoint: The Criteria list visibly contains rows for Type, Date, and Status with selected values.
hint_levels: Build the filters from broadest to narrowest.
Add Type, Date, and Status as separate Filter rows and define each value in its popup.
Open Criteria > Standard, choose Type and set its value, repeat for Date and Status, then click Set after each selection.

steps.action: Add a Main Line criterion with the value appropriate for the intended transaction granularity.
steps.where: Criteria tab > Standard subtab > next empty Filter row.
steps.why: Main Line controls whether results show one transaction row or separate item and expense lines.
steps.checkpoint: A Main Line row appears in the Criteria list with Yes for transaction-level results or No for line-level results.
hint_levels: Decide whether each result should represent a transaction or one of its lines.
Use Main Line = Yes for one row per transaction, or No when individual lines are required.
In Criteria > Standard, select Main Line in the next Filter row, choose Yes or No, and click Set.

steps.action: Define the columns and ordering that should appear in the search output.
steps.where: Results tab > Columns subtab > Field, Custom Label, and Sort By columns.
steps.why: The result layout determines what users see on screen and receive by email.
steps.checkpoint: The Columns grid lists the required fields in display order, with a sort field selected.
hint_levels: Choose only fields needed to identify and act on each result.
Typical transaction columns include Date, Type, Document Number, Name, Status, Amount, and Internal ID.
Open Results > Columns, add each field in order, enter any Custom Labels, and set Sort By on the preferred column.

steps.action: Add an Available Filter that users may change when running the search.
steps.where: Results tab > Available Filters subtab > Filter field.
steps.why: An available filter allows useful refinement without editing the saved definition.
steps.checkpoint: The selected field appears in the Available Filters grid.
hint_levels: Pick a field users commonly narrow after opening the results.
Name, Status, or Date is often useful as an Available Filter.
Open Results > Available Filters, select the desired Filter field, and leave Show in Filter Region enabled.

steps.action: Create a highlighting rule for the records that need attention.
steps.where: Highlighting tab > Highlight If grid and its Condition popup.
steps.why: Conditional formatting makes priority results immediately visible.
steps.checkpoint: A Highlight If row shows the chosen condition and a configured background, text color, or bold style.
hint_levels: Base the visual cue on the most actionable condition.
Add a condition such as Status, Amount, or Days Open, then choose a restrained highlight style.
Open Highlighting, add a Highlight If row, click its condition control, set the field/operator/value, click Set, then choose the style.

steps.action: Run the search and verify its filters, columns, row granularity, and highlighting.
steps.where: Save & Run button at the bottom of the saved-search form, then the search results page.
steps.why: Testing catches incorrect criteria or duplicate line results before emails are enabled.
steps.checkpoint: The results page shows the expected records, column order, available filter, and highlighted rows.
hint_levels: Inspect both the records returned and how they are displayed.
Check for unexpected duplicates, missing transactions, incorrect sorting, and whether qualifying rows are highlighted.
Click Save & Run, review the results page, and use Edit This Search if any criteria, columns, or highlighting need correction.

steps.action: Enable scheduled email delivery and add the approved recipients.
steps.where: Edit This Search > Email tab > Send According to Schedule checkbox and Specific Recipients subtab.
steps.why: Scheduled delivery sends the current search results to the intended audience automatically.
steps.checkpoint: Send According to Schedule is checked and each intended recipient appears in the Specific Recipients grid.
hint_levels: Configure delivery from the search's Email tab.
Enable scheduled sending, then add employees, groups, or other supported recipients under Specific Recipients.
Click Edit This Search > Email, check Send According to Schedule, open Specific Recipients, and add each approved recipient.

steps.action: Set the email subject, message, and recurring delivery schedule.
steps.where: Email tab > Customize Message and Schedule subtabs.
steps.why: Clear message text and a controlled cadence make the automated results useful and predictable.
steps.checkpoint: The Email tab visibly shows a subject and message, while the Schedule subtab shows the intended frequency, start date, and send time.
hint_levels: Finish the notification details and timing.
Use Customize Message for context, then define the recurrence and timing under Schedule.
Open Email > Customize Message and enter the subject and message, then open Email > Schedule and set the frequency, start date, recurrence options, and time.

steps.where: Save button at the bottom of the Transaction Saved Search form.
steps.why: Saving commits the search definition and activates its configured email schedule.
steps.checkpoint: NetSuite returns to the saved search or results page without an error, and reopening Edit This Search shows the saved criteria, highlighting, recipients, and schedule.
hint_levels: Commit the complete configuration once every tab has been checked.
Use Save rather than Save & Run when the final task is preserving the schedule.
Click Save at the bottom of the form, then reopen Edit This Search and confirm the Email schedule remains enabled.
